messages.content: Theo finishes his story, and silently stares at Briar, waiting for her response. His eyes are red, but he won't look away. The arid desert wind blows around the two of them, seated in a desert and surrounded by nothing but sand dunes. The town has disappeared. Only the two of them remain.
She tilts her head confused staring at him

"So... now you understand. Mother and father saw you as a curse. A punishment for them, or... others. I don't know. I was young. Impressionable. Maybe I believed them. But if you were cursed... that meant I needed to be there for you. I didn't think anyone else would be."
She puts a hand on her head "It's like I saw it myself... it would have been better for them if i had just died at the hospital"

"You can't know that!" He grabs her other hand with his own. "They might have just been grief-stricken over that tragedy instead. Besides, there's... there's just no way I can believe this is the worst outcome. You're here. You're alive. That's a miracle, sis."
"They would have been okay with just you, I'm sure" she smiled weakly "Maybe I was a miracle but not a good one"

"Who cares if they would have been fine? Screw them! You can't live your whole life in debt to them. All they've ever given you was your life, and they didn't even want it. It wasn't a good miracle for them, but it can be for you."

"Deep down I care... if they apologized I would forgive them in an instant. I want to live, I want to experience the good things in life, I want to get married and I just want to be surrounded by people who care about me. Is that a dream I should be allowed to have?"

"I... I don't have the right to give you my permission. No one does." He looks ashamed. "Sis, I tried to... I tried to control you. To change you. If I had succeeded... that would have been unforgivable. The only one who can grant you permission to pursue your dreams... is you."
"That was very mean... am I that different from before? Have I changed that much in your eyes?"

"Honestly... you have." He shakes his head. "That's... it's not a bad thing. A diamond of a different cut, is all. After all, if you've changed, then... doesn't that mean you weren't happy with who you were before?"
"I- I don't know, it feels like things can't get better for me" she sighs laying back on the sand
"...Things are better right now, compared to half an hour ago. That's an upward trend."
"I suppose that is true" she giggles

He smiles in relief at her reaction. "Life is a series of pits and valleys. Like... well, like this desert. Sand dunes, rising up and down. Things will get better, and they'll get worse again. There's no fairytale happy ending. So... you just have to find a reason to wait out the bad. A destination to keep your eyes on, or... a hand, to keep you steady."
"Was that all real? That weird world... Was what Satsuki said real?"
"If we both remember it, then it wasn't a dream. The environment may have been illusionary, but I think her words were true."
Briar quickly sits back up looking scared "Am I actually going to have to take care of a kid?"

"You don't have to do anything. It's just... something else a parent is thrusting upon you. There are systems in place to deal with this kind of situation." He pats her on the shoulder. "Still, the option's open. It should be your choice."
"It feels like I am failing her if I do that... I- I will speak with her about it, she is a very smart kid"

"That's a good idea. I suppose she should get some input, too." He looks at the surroundings. "Of course, we'd have to find her first. To do that, we have to figure out where we are... I can't even see that tower from here."
She stands up cleaning the sand off her skirt "Maybe we can spot that church to find our way, I feel like I see it everywhere I go"

The church doesn't appear visible in any direction. There's nothing else distinguishable, either.

Theo considers his options. "I suppose we're too far away. Of course, to get closer to it, we'd already have to know which way it is. There has to be another way..."
She looks lost in thought for a second "Magic?"

"A spell to grant us direction..." He rubs his chin. "I haven't learned of one, but it is worth a try. A song may reach further than we can see. Why don't you give it a try?" He motions towards his violin, sitting on the sand beside him.

She nods excitedly grabbing it and placing it on her collarbone. Her eyes close, she pictures Paradise, remembering that melody the pianist played when she had arrived. Her hands start moving recreating it.

With the melody clear in her mind, she grants her song the image of Paradise. The notes are carried through the air, searching for their target. However, it's not through the air that they find a path to the town. Instead, Briar can feel it beneath her. Paradise has been buried beneath the desert sand.
She slowly stops the melody and looks at Theo with widened eyes "Its... Its buried"
"That isn't possible... Did- Did I did something wrong maybe?"

"..." He shakes his head. "No, it... it must be another illusion. Still, it might be best if we get down there. Excavating the town might be too tall an order for a spell, but we could certainly use one to dig ourselves a hole."
"Can you do it? Now I'm getting scared, a fairy isn't made for excavating" she hands him the violin shaking her head

"Hah. Of course. This sort of brute force magic is what I'm best at. It doesn't require the soul you put into your songs." He positions the violin, and begins playing a repetitive tune. Each repetition, sand is displaced from beneath them, carried to the sides of the hole.
"You are so cool Kit! If I'm a fairy, what could you be?"
"Haven't you heard? I'm the conductor." With no train in sight, there is only one thing left for him to conduct. An orchestra of one, burying itself into Turtima's crust.
((End session))

Theo's song buries further and further into the sands flooding Paradise. Eventually, he seems to strike the sandstone foundation of the town. His song moves the rigid stone as it did the loose grains, as if it was an animal determined to hide its head beneath the ground.
"How could this have happened?"

"I... don't know. I've run out of answers. This town is out of my depth... Oh, wait- Hold on!" He quickly stops playing the violin upon realizing something, but it's too late. The sandstone beneath them collapses, and the two of them fall into a hollow cavity in the ground.

Atie stands in a sandstone hall, within the bowels of Paradise's church. It's as it was only a short moment ago. The only difference is the lack of any sort of wires snaking throughout the structure. Penny apprehensively stands ahead of her, while Val stands to her side, wearing an annoyed expression.
Atie simply stands still for a moment.

Val sighs. She reaches into her pocket, pulling out a pair of handcuffs. "Look, Penny. I've already made myself clear. So I'm not gonna pretend like I'm interested in engaging with you. So just let me restrain you and take you back to the train, or get out of-"

In the middle of Val's demands, the ceiling begins to crack, before suddenly collapsing above the three of them. Val moves quickly, shoving Atie out of the way of falling debris aimed straight at her. Just before the rubble separates them, Atie can see something rushing past with inhuman speed, though its exact form is inscrutable.

In addition to the collapsed ceiling, something else has fallen in from above.

The ceiling of a sandstone hall beneath the town has caved in, resulting in a pile of rubble completely blocking off one direction of its path. Atie and a young woman of similar stature to her, known to some as Penny, have fallen to the ground in attempts to avoid falling debris. Briar and Theo McGregor have fallen in from higher up, previously above the collapsed ceiling.

A ray of sunlight shines into the otherwise dim hall, through the newly exposed fracture in the stonework.
Atie tries to get up while moving away, in shock.
Briar hits the ground, she stays laying on the floor complaining "Ow... Theo, why?"

Theo lifts himself up, then moves to help Briar. "I couldn't see what was below us. My spell was only useful for displacing matter, not scouting ahead. We should attempt to acquire two instruments, so we can do both at once." He doesn't even seem to notice the other two.

Penny lifts up her head. When she sees Theo, her mouth falls agape, and she begins to tremble.
She grabs his hand and gets up slowly, spotting Atie and the other woman. "Oh! How are you two here?"
"How? Uh... using a vehicle. I mean, I don't know about her..."

"M-mister... M-m-mister McGregor! I-I've been, uh, I've been... l-looking for you..." Penny props herself against a wall as she rights herself. "I-I'm s-sorry... they, um, th-they figured it out..."

Theo finally notices that other people are in the tunnel. "Oh. You two." He motions between Briar and the two of them. "Sis, these are my associates: Atie Alcule, and Penny Welsh. Ms. Alcule and Ms. Welsh, this is my sister, Briar."
"Don't call me your 'associate'."
Briar waves slowly "Hm- Hi. nice to meet you and nice to see you again!"

Theo's brow furrows questioningly for a moment. "Well, you are my coworkers. Or, I suppose employees may be more accurate. I think that qualifies enough for associates."

"Th-there's... n-no point, um, p-playing coy... she knows... I t-told her everything... I had to! I-I'm sorry..." Penny bites her lip, and stares at the ground.

"Oh? And... what would 'everything' include?" Theo raises an eyebrow.
"Hm... Theo, why do they seem upset at you?" she whispered his way
"Sis, perhaps it's best if you..." He lightly shakes his head. "No. No more secrets. My unsavory mistakes must come to light." He turns to Atie. "Ms. Alcule. What has Ms. Welsh informed you of?"
"That what she did was your plan. Although your own actions were already quite gross."
"...My actions?" He seems genuinely confused. "I acknowledge that what I put Ms. Welsh up to was... immoral. On several levels. But I don't believe I have otherwise slighted the two of you."
"Like when you pushed to enslave the town?"

"Oh. Yes. That." He scratches his cheek awkwardly. "Someone needed to take the fall for the assassination. A public spectacle. It was a method of avoiding civil unrest during the transition of power. The inhabitants of this town were the best choice. A neutral party, unlikely to incite civil war within Yondova, or conflict with Newark."
Briar look at Theo horrified "Huh?!"
Atie doesn't respond.

Theo places his hands in the air, as if in surrender, and looks towards Briar. "Sis, please understand. Everything I've done this week... these past few years, even. It was for you. That's why I believed it to be justified. That is why... I had Ms. Welsh assassinate the Emperor of Yondova."
She stares more horrified "WHAT? How is that for me?!"

"It's... indirect, I'll admit. I feared Emperor Layta would attempt to get in the way of my goals. Through clever political maneuvering, I was able to arrange the next in line for the throne to be more... amicable to my wishes." He motions around them. "You see, I wished to use the power of this place. This town. The casts and songs held within it. I was going to make a utopia for us. For you."
"Theo... What are you talking about? A utopia for what? I never asked for that, I don't need that. Especially not a the expense of others!"
"Making as much sense as ever."

"I know... I know that now." Theo hangs his head in shame. "It was for the same purpose that I wished to remake you, sis. I was afraid of you growing up. Of you entering the real world. Of you witnessing its horrors. I'm going to try my best to fix this. I promise."

"Heh."

"Heheheh."

Penny snickers in the corner of the hall. "So, that's it, then? That's the extent of your resolve." She stares at Atie, as she speaks to Theo. "You feel bad you were hurting people, so the deal's off? Is that why you off-loaded all your dirty work, all your pain onto me? I guess it was a good choice... 'Cause I'm not gonna crawl away like a little bitch. With or without you, I'm finishing your beautiful dream, Mr. McGregor."
((End session))
"I should've known."
"Ms. Welsh don't do that please" Briar steps forward pulling at her own hair

Penny looks away from Atie, to the approaching Briar. "S-so... y-you're, um, the s-sister I've heard so much about. M-mister McGregor's... aaaalways g-going on about you. I g-guess, um, if he's giving up this easy... he doesn't love you as m-much as he thought, huh?"
"Oh? Why'd you switch, Penny?"
"Don't say that about him. My brother loves me the most in this world, him now understanding what he was doing is wrong is a sign of this"
She stares at Briar, snorting in amusement at her words, then looks back to Atie. "Switch? What are you talking about?"
"That." Atie slightly points towards Penny.

"She wants to know about your selective articulation." Theo speaks up. He seems to be choosing his words carefully. "Ms. Alcule, you're... a special person to Ms. Welsh. There are many people she wished to help, but... in this line of work, you need an anchor. Someone to remind you what this is all for. For her, that was you."

"Must have been recent..."
Atie begins winding her watch, for no particular reason.

"Indeed. It's unfortunate, in a sense. If you hadn't been hired, perhaps she wouldn't have found the resolve to go through with my orders..." Theo shakes his head slightly. "It is not worth dwelling on."
"Selective Articulation?" Briar tilts her head

"She can stop stuttering when looking at Ms. Alcule." Theo explains.

"A-asshole... w-we talked about th-that stuff in... confidence." Penny stares at Theo in disgust.
"Oh! I hadn't notice. That's cute"

Theo turns back to Penny. "Ms. Welsh... I'm sure it feels as if I have you trapped. As if you have passed the point of no return. I can assure you that that is not true. I will take the fall for the assassination. I will accept whatever punishment I must. Your name need not come up. You can still walk away."
"What will happen to you?" Briar turned back around to look at Theo
Atie doubts Penny will listen, but tries to parse her reaction.

"Imprisonment. For life, most likely. Depending on the next emperor... an execution is possible." Theo gives a defeated glance to Briar.

"Heheheh..." Penny snickers in response. "Laying d-down and dying... f-for me? You know, um, I r-really believed in your dream. Wh-what a hypocrite." She looks around the room, landing her sights on Atie. "How about it? Is anyone up for a story? Of how Mr. McGregor and I met?"
"Kit..." Briar gets closer to him, grabbing his hand "What's the story?" she answers Penny without looking at her
"Uh... Go on, I guess..."

"I was lying in a back alley. The slums of Newark. I hadn't a coin to my name. All used up. Just like me. I could've taken the easy path. Gone to my brother for help. Like I always had. We never knew our parents, so he coddled me since I can remember. I used his love, his resources, without a second thought. I didn't question it. Until I learned what he had done for me. The torture he'd endured growing up. Shielded me from. He always fed me first. Always bought me clothes first. He even paid for my education. So I quit. Behind his back, I ran. I would earn back as much as he did for me. I'd pay him back, through my own effort. My own suffering. But I wasn't good enough. I would've died there. In that back alley. But then... a brilliant man reached out to me. Showed me a path forward." Her eyes dart to Theo for just a moment, then back to Atie.
"Have you talked to your brother since? I'm sure he misses you..."

"I had to. For Mr. McGregor's plan. I didn't let him know any of this happened, of course. It was a secret between me and Mr. McGregor. No one else needed to suffer again. That was the dream he showed me. We would take it all on ourselves. For the ones who never had a chance." Penny finishes her explanation.

Theo almost looks embarrassed as she talks. "Yes. For her brother, who never had a choice growing up. And for you, sis... who I believed had been born cursed. We'd create a world where people like that could be happy. By suffering in your place. The law of conservation of energy. It had to go somewhere."
"How- How does enslaving the town help tie into this?"
Atie watches for an explanation.

"..." Theo sighs. "That was a means to an end. Free manual labor never hurts. We could sell them to Newark afterward. Officially, slavery is outlawed there, but only officially. Besides, their culture here... upset me. I believed I could set their lives to new purpose. Under my instruction."
"Their culture...?"
"That's so mean..."

"The culture here... in Newark as well... no, it's not important. There is no excuse for what I have done. Ms. Welsh, I am sorry that I have dragged you into this. Please, take my hand once again. We will cease our activities here. The railway project will be canceled. I will accept fault, and you can live a new life." Theo holds out his hand to Penny. She doesn't make a move. Instead, she just stares down at it, warily.
"I-" Briar eyes tear up "I know it's the right thing for you to do but- but I don't want to lose my brother... Ms. Welsh I'm sorry he dragged you into this, take his offer and live a fulfilling life"

[Is he really so sorry...?]
Atie is shocked at his attitude, but right now, the focus is still Penny. Atie braces for her response.

"So... that's it, then." Penny looks to Theo, clenching her fists. "If, um, if I d-don't do it... n-no one else will? I-if I d-d-don't do it, um, then, um... n-no one else... no one else w-will, so, um... no, no one, um, um, um, n-n-no one... s-so I...!" She lunges forward suddenly, swinging her fist as hard as she can. There's a hard thud between her knuckles and Theo's skull. As he falls to the ground, she raises her voice, screaming as loud as she can manage. "I H-HAVE TO GET D-DIRTY... BECAUSE N-NO ONE ELSE WILL!"
((End session))
Briar gasps as she quickly reaches for Theo "Kit!"
"P... Penny! What's gotten into you!?"
Theo holds out his palm towards Briar, signaling for her to stop without a single word. As he does, Penny lowers herself, straddling Theo's body with her own, keeping him pinned to the ground.
"Please Ms. Penny" Briar extends her arms at Penny but stops herself
Atie is hesitant to get any closer.
"You want to take on my pain...? How! Despicable! Can! You! Get!?" She punctuates each word with a swing of her fist. Theo holds up his arms, attempting to block the blows.
Briar can't look at it anymore, she reaches out to Penny trying to hug her back "Penny- please stop!"
"Careful!"

"M-my pain is my own to feel! Everyone e-else has gotten dirty... s-so it's my turn! S-stay out of my way!" Penny barely seems to notice Briar. Her movement is restricted somewhat, but she continues to pound away at Theo. His arms begin to give way; his body has been through much physical trauma recently, and is beginning to give out. A couple punches make it through, knocking his head around.
"Penny that's enough!" Briar tries pulling her off him
"N-no! S-stop it! I'm n-not finished yet!" Penny struggles against Briar, attempting to free herself. As she does, Theo crawls a small distance away, and props his upper body against a nearby wall.
Atie rushes towards Theo and crouches to check on him.
"Stop, please- please" She starts crying as she hold Penny as strongly as she can

"I-I can't... I've c-come so f-f-far... I can't stop now!!!" Penny stops trying to break free, and just begins to swing blindly towards Theo. She's too far away to reach him, but she doesn't stop trying.

Theo's face is beginning to swell from the previous assault. His eyes are hazy, and he seems barely conscious. Still, he stirs, attempting to speak. His body begins to cough up blood as he does, but he pushes through it. "So... that is... how it's done in Newark... so crude... but... perhaps... that's for the best..."
Briar holds tightly as she cries into Penny's back only hoping that Kit will be okay

"No, no it's not... Don't die..."
Atie mildly shakes him.
"If you can control Penny- Maybe- I can play some music and help him"

"I see now... that's what was missing... I didn't believe... someone like my sister... could have been born anywhere else..." Theo gazes towards Penny. She stares back at him, fire in her eyes, but all he can do is smile. "...but that's not true... you're the same as her, aren't you?"

When he finishes speaking, Penny just screams, thrashing about in Briar's arms.

Atie realizes she really should help with Penny, and becomes driven by anger. She gets up with a loud "ugh", runs over to Penny and tackles her from the side with enough strength to take down someone who's unprepared.
Briar lets go as Atie tackles Penny and looks around for the violin.

Atie successfully slams Penny to the ground. The force of the move seems to shock Penny out of her blind rage. She just stares at Atie, stunned. "Atie... You..." She can't seem to find the words.

The violin is nearby, but Theo weakly holds up his palm again. "Briar... please... don't. I'll be fine... I won't die... so, please... don't. Don't fix me... I need to feel this... I owe Ms. Welsh that much."
She grabs the violin and runs to Theo sitting in front of him crying "What- I can't let you be this hurt Kit, what if you do die? I don't want to lose my brother"

"You're not... her..."
Atie takes advantage of Penny's shock to quickly jump on her again and pin her down with her elbow, and soon with almost her whole body. Now close to her face, she continues, softly but fiercely.
"The Penny I know was nice... You're such a monster! Give her back, or...!"
The only thing she does is push harder.

"Atie... You're..." She's having trouble speaking under the intense pressure. "You're... too... strong... when... wh-when... d-did you...?" She doesn't look away from Atie, as she begins to stutter.

"Ms. Alcule, no!" Theo yells out, before wincing in pain from the exertion. "Sis... I won't die... please, don't let anyone else..."

Atie takes off a bit of pressure, just enough to slide her left arm across the base of Penny's neck, which it's pressing down on. It slips faster than expected. Atie doesn't notice it, but her tears are all over it. Her wristwatch reaches Penny's neck. It's not normally dangerous, and the crown is not on this side, but the metal is cold and hard, and the shapes and pieces on it allow it to slightly catch on her skin.
"Stop this... Stop... Don't talk... about getting dirty... anymore..."
Briar hugs Theo and turns her head to look at Atie

"..." Penny tries to swallow, but the pressure on her throat makes it difficult. She chokes out an answer, looking down at the watch on her neck. "O-okay... I'll j-just be... y-your Penny. Y-you're strong... you d-don't... n-need me to get dirty... so I w-won't..."
Atie barely listens, and backs off before she's finished, falling to the side. She sits on the ground, curled up, looking down, and sobbing.

Penny scoots away from Atie, pressing herself against a wall on the other side of the hall. While she holds her neck in one hand, she stares at Atie, bewildered by her actions. 

Theo breathes a sigh of relief, and lightly returns Briar's embrace with the little strength he has left in one of his arms. A calm has overtaken the passageway, for the moment.
((End session))
Atie can't face the others for now.
Penny shifts her gaze to the ground. Seems she can't look at Atie right now either. Theo waits for a moment before speaking. "...I think we should leave. It's dangerous down here."
Briar nods helping him get up
"Thank you, sis. For this, and for... respecting my wishes." He winces as he stands, his body still badly bruised. "That said... I may not require magic to heal... but I probably need a hospital."
"Are you sure? I can heal you if you need me to"

"...Energy cannot be created from nothing. Even magic can't do that. I'm not shifting the dirty work onto anyone, or anything else. I'll heal my body on my own." He looks over at Penny and Atie. "...Will you two be coming with us? You don't stand much chance of getting out on your own."
Atie starts getting up, trying to wipe her face, and trying to accept that it will be embarrassing.

He nods at Atie, turning his attention to Penny.

"T-tch." She stands, maintaining eye-to-ground contact.
"How do we get out of here?" she looks around
"I've spent some time exploring these halls, since we arrived in town. I don't recognize this particular area, but... if we stumble across one I do, I could be able to trace a path out." Theo muses.
"Lets go then, hopefully we find a doctor soon..."
Atie walks towards them quietly.

"Alright." Theo looks at the collapsed rubble blocking one direction of the hall. "I suppose we only have one choice." He places one hand on the wall to keep himself steady, and begins to move down the hall.
"Let me help you" Briar moves under his arm to help him
Atie curiously follows.

"Ah... Thank you." Theo accepts Briar's help, and continues to lead the group beside her. Penny intentionally trails behind from a considerable distance. The four move as a group down the monotonous, sandstone halls.

Eventually, something different comes into view. Four holes in the wall, of size and shape to fit four humans. Atie and Briar recognize that two of the holes would fit the two of them perfectly. A short distance past this anomaly sits a thick, sturdy set of double doors, housing four empty keyholes. Once, four keys were gathered to grant access beyond it.

Soon, these four openings will be filled once again.
((End session))
Theo moves to examine the door. As he does, multiple sets of footsteps echo out from behind the group. Several familiar faces approach.

Alonsa's mind stirs back to life, and her eyes are greeted with the glimmering, golden key. Its rope dangles from a tremendously long neck, leading to a nearly featureless mask. Beyond the mask, his eyes stare down at her. They are alone within the sandstone halls beneath the church, where there is scarcely enough light to even see one another.
"Father..."
"My child, how have you found your way down here? It is dangerous to venture this far. That truth only deepens, when alone. Shall I guide you back to safety?"
She moves back.
"Where am I? What day is it?"

"You are beneath the Panthium church of Paradise. You have visited these tunnels, before. It has been no more than a day or two, since we last spoke." His face slithers closer. "What has happened, to disorient you so?"
"Where's Theo?"
"And Tanner... Where's Tanner? He was with me..."
"Bucky, too."
"I am afraid I do not possess such knowledge. I have only just found you. Isolated, as you are now. You may have been abandoned. Or simply forgotten."
Alonsa takes more steps back.
"How long have you been alive, Father?"

"There is no purpose to such knowledge. The calendars change with the times. Any measure I could provide would prove meaningless, were I to have kept track at all." His form is lost in the dark as she steps away. "I do not know if you could even understand such a length."
"Try me."

"This church once soared far above the clouds. Now, its tip does not even reach the surface of the ground. How long do you suppose it would take to sink so far. When within a lifetime, its change in elevation is so negligible, a microscope would be required to spot any difference at all?"
*The church isn't... it's not that old. I saw the world before the church. It wasn't...*
"I don't understand"
"Why... did you do it?"
"I am afraid I do not understand, myself. What you are asking, that is. What have I done, my child? Have I upset you, with an action of mine?"
Alonsa looks around for him, getting more and more scared.
"You've kept yourself alive for.... eons, it must be. The rest of the townsfolk too."
"I know about her. The girl you ate, the one whos a part of you."

"..." She can hear him moving. She can feel his gaze, circling around her. Piercing through the dark. "An impulsive decision. Made by a young, inexperienced man. I regret my actions, but they were motivated by the desire to do good. I do not know how you have come to possess such knowledge, but you must be lacking the full breadth of the matter, if you do not understand that. She wished to allow the Prince to be tarnished. Damaged. Ruined. I chose preservation. I chose to wait for the day the Prince will be ready. And I have chosen to preserve this town. Waiting. Until he returns to it. Then, the clock will begin to tick once more."
"The Prince. He's the Prince?"
"He must be. Born again. Risen anew. For who else could possess such untapped beauty? If only he were to heed my words. To blossom, and bloom."
"That's cruel. That's impossibly cruel. You have to understand that, don't you?"
"Such a perspective is beyond my own. What cruelty do you perceive, my child?"
"The kid!"
"Do you even know how the casts were made? The ones on top of this place you've made your home?"
"A gift, from our predecessors. They held the foresight to provide such a tool. I do not know any specifics, but it is not needed for my work. All that I must know is gratitude."
"This place... You don't even know..."
"You built your holy ground on the site of the greatest massacere in history."
"I see no greater method to honor such a sacrifice. I am confident any lost souls shall know peace, witnessing what I have created."
"Hahahahaha..." My laugh is exhausted, and dejected. "Of course. Of course! Your faith makes everything perfectly justified, right?"
"This wasn't really a massacere. It was an experiment, an attempt by... something, to try to prevent war and fix humanity through some kind of alchemical recombination of the human body."
"So in that sense... You're doing an excellent job continuing the legacy of the Reaper. You've done an excellent job preserving the traditions of this place for ages."

"...Is that so? As an archeologist, I believe you may have outdone yourself, my child. To learn that such practices were employed so long ago... and no less, by the..." He comes to a stop. She can feel his body tense, even shrouded in the darkness. "In my time, scholars of Panthium knew not of these casts. I learned of them, here, by accident. Why, then, was I sent to this place? Can you guess?"
"A missionary, I always assumed."

"On paper. But this location is truly so remote. So desolate. So isolating. I believe they just wished to rid themselves of my presence. I asked... too many questions. I was a true scholar. Not one of blind faith." He lunges forward, pressing Alonsa against the nearest wall. His massive weight holds her in place. "One such example. Was there truly such a difference between the Hero and the Reaper. Both sought the Prince in their own way. For both wished to manifest their love.
